summary: The Settings and Quick Access windows fail to appear on Windows 10 while the rest of PowerToys remains available; the latest discussion links a newer report with the same symptom.

status.label: Duplicate Windows 10 UI-launch investigation
status.detail: The report matches the still-open canonical investigation in #40234; no separate fix path is evidenced.

next_action.label: Link the canonical investigation
next_action.reason: Consolidate this report with #40234, which covers the same Settings and Quick Access launch failure on Windows 10.

judgment.rationale: Issue #40234 records the same Windows 10 behavior: the tray and enabled utilities remain available, while Settings and Quick Access briefly show a wait cursor and never display. A PowerToys member closed the similar Settings-only issue #41292 as a duplicate of #40234. The latest comment on this issue also links #50335, an open Settings report with the same symptom but no maintainer-confirmed fix.
evidence: The issue reports PowerToys 0.90.0 on Windows 10, where both Settings and Quick Access do not open after a brief busy cursor; a second Windows 10 user confirmed the behavior.
The issue includes a diagnostic ZIP attachment and has no assignee; its live labels are Issue-Bug, Product-Settings, and Needs-Triage.
Issue #40234 remains open and describes Settings, Quick Access, and other UI windows failing to appear on Windows 10 while PowerToys itself continues running.
A PowerToys member closed #41292 as a duplicate of #40234, explicitly identifying the same Settings UI launch failure.
The latest comment links #50335, whose reporter describes the same Windows 10 Settings failure and a CET/runtime hypothesis; that hypothesis has not been confirmed by a maintainer.
judgment.recommended_action: Post the proposed consolidation comment linking the active canonical investigation #40234.

fix_assessment.rationale: A separate PowerToys code-fix proposal is not applicable to this duplicate report. The matching canonical investigation #40234 remains open, and the only CET explanation supplied in linked issue #50335 is user-provided rather than a confirmed root cause or an existing fix.

issue_context.summary: On Windows 10 with PowerToys 0.90.0, opening Settings by double-clicking and opening Quick Access both show a short busy cursor but no window. Another Windows 10 user reports the same behavior, and the newest comment links a current matching Settings report.
known_information: The reporter identifies PowerToys 0.90.0 installed from GitHub on Windows 10 with an AMD Ryzen 7 5800H and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060.
The reported failure affects both the Settings window and Quick Access, whereas PowerToys Run is in active use.
A PowerToys diagnostic ZIP was attached to this issue, but its contents were not needed to establish the duplicate relationship.
The issue has no assignee and remains labeled Issue-Bug, Product-Settings, and Needs-Triage.
Issue #40234 is an open Windows 10 report with the same Settings and Quick Access failure pattern, and #41292 was closed by a member as its duplicate.
The latest comment links #50335, where a user reports the same symptom and attributes it to a Windows 10/.NET CET compatibility problem.
inferences: This issue is very likely part of the same Windows 10 UI-launch failure family tracked by #40234, but the exact failing mechanism for this machine is not confirmed.
Because the runner launches PowerToys.Settings.exe for both Settings and Quick Access, failure during that application's startup could explain the shared symptom; this does not prove a CET cause.
issue_context.analysis: The public symptom overlap is specific: #40234 describes a running PowerToys instance whose Settings and Quick Access UI paths show a brief wait state and never appear, matching this issue. The duplicate handling of #41292 by a PowerToys member provides public triage precedent. Focused source review shows the tray routes both actions through open_settings_window, which launches PowerToys.Settings.exe, but the report lacks a crash record that would identify a source-level defect. The CET explanation in #50335 is useful context and is corroborated by the separate open CET report #47814, yet neither establishes this report's root cause or a fix. Consolidating with #40234 avoids a competing unverified design.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue body, both comments, live labels, assignees, and timeline; no linked pull request, closing event, or assigned owner exists.
Reviewed #50335 in full: it is open, has the same labels, and contains an unconfirmed user investigation of a CET/runtime crash.
Reviewed #40234 and #41292 in full: #40234 remains the active matching Windows 10 UI-launch investigation, and a member closed #41292 as its duplicate.
Reviewed related public work: merged PR #37550 disabled CETCompat only for PowerToys Run's launcher and does not establish a fix for the Settings application.

Reviewed current runner ownership and history: src/runner/tray_icon.cpp routes Settings and Quick Access to open_settings_window; src/runner/settings_window.cpp starts WinUI3Apps/PowerToys.Settings.exe with CreateProcessW. Recent Settings/runner changes have contributors including Niels Laute and Boliang Zhang, but no matching active fix was found.

actions.label: Link the canonical Windows 10 UI-launch investigation

comment.body: Thanks for linking #50335. This report's pattern--PowerToys remains running, while opening Settings and Quick Access briefly shows a busy cursor and no window--matches the active Windows 10 UI-launch investigation in #40234. A similar Settings-only report, #41292, was closed by a PowerToys member as a duplicate of #40234. Please consolidate follow-up evidence there; #50335 has a useful user-supplied CET/runtime hypothesis, but it is not yet a maintainer-confirmed root cause or fix.
